info.name: VectorFilter
info.comment: Constructs filter pipelines that alter rendered vector graphics.

description.p: The VectorFilter class allows post-effect filters to be applied to vectors as they are being rendered. Filter support is closely modelled around the SVG standard, and effect results are intended to match that of the standard. Once created, a filter can be utilised by vector objects through their Vector.Filter field. By way of example in SVG:

Filter pipelines are constructed from effects based on the FilterEffect class, such as CompositeFX and FloodFX. Construct a new pipeline by creating effect objects and placing them under the ownership of the VectorFilter that will be supporting them. The VectorFilter will detect the filter objects and they will be processed in the order in which they are added. It is most optimal to create each pipeline in advance, and a new VectorFilter object should be created for each pipeline as necessary.

The filter's output is composited into the target with the blend mode resolved for the client vector, as described for Vector.ColourSpace, and the filter's Opacity is applied at the same time. The filter's own ColourSpace governs effect processing only and does not affect how the output is composited.

Effects can read content that lies beyond the edges of the page, within the filter region, so a filtered vector that touches or crosses a page edge is processed as if the page were larger. Samples outside of the filter region are transparent black. The output is clipped to the page and any clipping imposed by container viewports.

It is important to note that filter effects are CPU intensive tasks and real-time performance may be disappointing. If this is an issue, consider pre-rendering the filter effects in advance and caching the results in memory or files.
It is a requirement that VectorFilter objects are owned by the VectorScene they are targeting.

field.name: AspectRatio
field.comment: Selects per-axis or diagonal scaling for bounding box units.

description.p: AspectRatio affects the filter region when Units is BOUNDING_BOX, and the effects that support it when PrimitiveUnits is BOUNDING_BOX. The default is MEET, which scales horizontal values by the width of the bounding box and vertical values by its height, as per the SVG standard.

The NONE option is a Kōtuku extension that scales all values by the normalised diagonal of the bounding box, i.e. sqrt(width^2 + height^2) / sqrt(2). This is the same formula used by a scaled stroke width. A blur radius or offset then covers the same distance on both axes for any shape, which is preferable for effects such as glows and drop shadows. For the filter region, the X, Y, Width and Height values are measured from the edges of the bounding box, so the default region adds a margin of 10% of the normalised diagonal to every side.
The following effects support NONE: BlurFX, LightingFX and OffsetFX.

field.name: ColourSpace
field.comment: The colour space of the filter graphics (SRGB or linear RGB).

description.p: By default, colour filters are processed in SRGB format. This is the same colour space as used by the rest of the graphics system, which means that no special conversion is necessary prior to and post filter processing. However, linear RGB is better suited for producing high quality results at a cost of speed.

Intermediate images are always stored in sRGB encoding. When LINEAR_RGB is selected, effects that honour this setting decode their inputs, process them in linear RGB and encode the result for storage. These are BlurFX, ColourFX, ConvolveFX, DisplacementFX (for the displacement map), LightingFX, MergeFX, MorphologyFX, RemapFX and the ARITHMETIC operator of CompositeFX. The other CompositeFX operators that mix colour components always do so in linear RGB. Colours that are input values, such as the colour of a FloodFX, are stored as given and are not converted.
This setting applies only to the processing of effects within the pipeline. The composite of the filter's output into the target is governed by the client vector's Vector.ColourSpace.

The SVG standard defaults to linear RGB for filter effects, so the SVG parser selects LINEAR_RGB unless the color-interpolation-filters attribute states otherwise. Filters created through the API retain the SRGB default.

field.name: EffectXML
field.comment: Returns a SVG XML string that defines the filter's effects.

description.p: This field value will return a purpose-built string that defines the filter's effects in SVG compliant XML.

field.name: Height
field.comment: The height of the filter area. Can be expressed as a fixed or scaled coordinate.

description.p: The height of the filter area is expressed here as a fixed or scaled coordinate. The Width and Height effectively restrain the working space for the effect processing, making them an important consideration for efficiency.

The coordinate system for the width and height depends on the value for Units. In bounding-box mode, the AspectRatio determines whether the value is relative to the bounding box or its normalised diagonal.
The default values for Width and Height is 120%, as per the SVG standard. This provides a buffer space for the filter algorithms to work with, and is usually a sufficient default.

field.name: Inherit
field.comment: Inherit attributes from a VectorFilter referenced here.

description.p: Attributes can be inherited from another filter by referencing that gradient in this field. This feature is provided primarily for the purpose of simplifying SVG compatibility and its use may result in an unnecessary performance penalty.
The opacity of the filter is defined as a value between 0.0 and 1.0, with 1.0 being fully opaque. The default value is 1.0.

field.name: PrimitiveUnits
field.comment: Alters the behaviour of some effects that support alternative position calculations.

description.p: PrimitiveUnits alters the behaviour of some effects when their dimensions are calculated. The default value is USERSPACE. When set to BOUNDING_BOX, the effect may calculate its dimensions strictly based on the client vector using a scaled coordinate space of (0, 0, 100%, 100%).

field.name: ResX
field.comment: Width of the intermediate images, measured in pixels.

description.p: The combination of ResX and ResY define the available space for rendering of filter effects. It is recommended that the client does not set these values because the default 1:1 pixel ratio is appropriate in the majority of circumstances.

field.name: ResY
field.comment: Height of the intermediate images, measured in pixels.

description.p: The combination of ResX and ResY define the available space for rendering of filter effects. It is recommended that the client does not set these values because the default 1:1 pixel ratio is appropriate in the majority of circumstances.

field.name: Units
field.comment: Defines the coordinate system for X, Y, Width and Height.

description.p: The default coordinate system is BOUNDING_BOX, which positions the filter within the client vector. The alternative is USERSPACE, which positions the filter relative to the client vector's nearest viewport.

field.name: Width
field.comment: The width of the filter area. Can be expressed as a fixed or scaled coordinate.

description.p: The width of the filter area is expressed here as a fixed or scaled coordinate. The Width and Height effectively restrain the working space for the effect processing, making them an important consideration for efficiency.

The coordinate system for the width and height depends on the value for Units. In bounding-box mode, the AspectRatio determines whether the value is relative to the bounding box or its normalised diagonal.
The default values for Width and Height is 120%, as per the SVG standard. This provides a buffer space for the filter algorithms to work with, and is usually a sufficient default.

The meaning of the (X, Y) field values depend on the value for Units. In userspace mode, the filter position will be relative to the client vector's parent viewport. In bounding-box mode, the filter position is relative to the vector's position, and the AspectRatio determines whether the value is relative to the bounding box or its normalised diagonal. It is important to note that coordinates are measured before any transforms are applied.
The default values for X and Y is 10%, as per the SVG standard. This provides a buffer space for the filter algorithms to work with, and is usually a sufficient default.

The meaning of the (X, Y) field values depend on the value for Units. In userspace mode, the filter position will be relative to the client vector's parent viewport. In bounding-box mode, the filter position is relative to the vector's position, and the AspectRatio determines whether the value is relative to the bounding box or its normalised diagonal. It is important to note that coordinates are measured before any transforms are applied.
The default values for X and Y is 10%, as per the SVG standard. This provides a buffer space for the filter algorithms to work with, and is usually a sufficient default.

constants.const: Inherit the colour space option from the parent vector.
Operate in linear light. This produces higher quality results, and is the SVG default for color-interpolation-filters.
Operate on sRGB-encoded values directly. This is the fastest option, and is the SVG default for color-interpolation.

constants.comment: Define the aspect ratio for VectorFilter unit scaling.
constants.const: Scale X/Y values independently and in relation to the width/height of the bounding box.
Scale X/Y values on a 1:1 basis, in relation to the normalised diagonal of the bounding box.
Coordinates are scaled to the object's bounding box.
Either the default setting will be applied or the setting will be inherited from a parent object.
Coordinates are scaled to the current viewport.
